newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end up after limit gain on cash outlook.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end up after limit gain on cash outlook.

text.p: Optimism that he cash market may finally start its seasonal spring rally supported CME lumber futures with short covering boosting May up the daily limit before prices ended sharply higher, traders said.
May had posted a limit gain of $10.00 per thousand board feet at $382.90 before closing $8.50 higher at $381.40 and July up $5.60 at $372.80 per tbf. Other months ended $4.30 to $2.00 higher.

Cash activity increased late Tuesday in studs and there was talk that this will be the start of the spring home building season and increased demand for lumber. Cash trade had been slow for some time, traders said.

"There is better cash market activity and the hope that it's more than a one day wonder, which is all we had so far this year, I think is what has created the buying in the futures," said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading.
Traders said commission house and fund buying sparked buy stops in May when it pushed through the 40-day average around $378. May ran up the limit before profit taking pared gains.
Prudential Securities, Cargill Investor Services, Smith Barney and Refco bought on the rally, pit sources said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $367 per tbf, off $5 from Friday and $9 under the previous midweek level. They said many dealers continued to anticipate heavier lumber offerings in April from Canadian mills, even though most secondaries and producers disagreed. However, improving weather was boosting consumption.
